claims.hypothesis: Is [C II] detectable in a stack of faint lensed z~6 galaxies, and does it follow the local L[CII]-SFR relation?
claims.experiment: Weighted-average and median LINESTACKER stacking of 52 sources (plus three sub-samples) in ALCS cubes
claims.result: No detection; 3 sigma L[CII] upper limits of (1-9)e7 Lsun
claims.finding: Limits imply a deviation towards lower L[CII] than the local relation, though median-stack limits remain marginally compatible and biases could underestimate the limits

evidence.quote: Our analyses find no detection of either
Compared to the local $L_{\rm [CII]}$-SFR relation, this implies a deviation towards lower $L_{\rm [CII]}$, similar to previous results for individual detections of $z>6$ lensed galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: How much of the star formation in these galaxies is obscured by dust?
claims.experiment: Continuum stacking with modified blackbody (T=35, 45 K, beta=1.5), converting L_FIR upper limits to SFR_IR
claims.result: No continuum detection; SFR_IR upper limit ~1-6 Msun/yr after magnification correction, similar to or below SFR_UV
claims.finding: Less than half of the star formation is obscured

evidence.quote: This implies that less than half of the star formation is obscured by dust.

claims.hypothesis: What molecular gas content do the [C II] upper limits imply?
claims.experiment: Applied the Madden et al. L[CII]-M_H2 recipe and compared to SED stellar masses
claims.result: M_H2 upper limits of 1.3e9 to 7.0e9 Msun; f_molgas upper limits about 0.5 (mean) and 0.9 (median)
claims.finding: M_H2 is of order or higher than the stellar mass, consistent with Dessauges-Zavadsky et al. at similar stellar mass

evidence.quote: these suggest that $M_{\rm H_2}$ is of the order of or higher than $M_{\rm stellar}$

claims.hypothesis: Why do mean and median stacks give different L[CII]-SFR positions?
claims.experiment: Compared mean and median stacked cubes and the sample magnifications and SFRs
claims.result: Stacked cubes have comparable rms; the upper limits differ because the weighted-mean and median magnifications differ
claims.finding: Magnification and SFR derivation dominate the difference between mean and median results

evidence.quote: This is not due to a drastic difference in the resulting stacked cubes, but comes essentially from the difference between the mean and median magnification of our sample.

why_this_data.value: Cluster fields give lensing amplification to reach faint sub-L* z>6 galaxies

evidence.quote: observations can be done more efficiently by targeting galaxy cluster fields as gravitational lensing will amplify the light from such distant galaxies

why_this_method.value: Stacking improves sensitivity for individually undetected galaxies

evidence.quote: the stacking of the data can enable a significant statistical improvement in the sensitivity

evidence.quote: leading to a heterogeneous sample

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits depend strongly on adopted lens models and per-source SFR (mean vs median differ mainly through magnification)
Individual redshift offsets (Ly-alpha vs [C II]) are not modelled; no injection-recovery test of the stack
Sample of Ly-alpha emitters is biased and heterogeneous, so conclusions about the general z~6 population are weak
Single tapered beam assumed to cover all sources; source sizes and extended [C II] not tested beyond a native-resolution check
